title: Setup alignment: align the part by picking three points onto a plane

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Proposed by the maintainer (filed by an agent), 2026-11-09: "a option to align on three points is probably more sane, if we gonna have several ways of aligning a model to a workplane."

**What:** a setup alignment mode that picks three points on the model (vertices or points on faces). The three points define a plane, which is laid onto the chosen G17/G18/G19 plane like "face to plane" (#330): the plane's normal is rotated onto the work plane's normal, the model is translated so the plane lies in it, and the part stays on the correct side. Optionally, point 1 becomes the origin and point 1 to 2 sets the X direction (a full 3-point frame, the common shop "3-2-1" setup).

**Why:** it works on parts with no single clean face (castings, freeform, scanned meshes), and it avoids the face/edge snapping problem.

**Requirements:**
- It goes through one undoable command, validated at creation, and refuses by name: points that are collinear or too close (a degenerate plane), non-finite input, or no model.
- It uses the same apply path as face-to-plane, so the two can't disagree.
- Setup page UI: pick points 1, 2 and 3 with a clear prompt and a clear/redo.

**Done means:** tests for three points on a tilted face laying it flat on G17 (normal -Z, z = 0, part above); collinear points refused by name; undo restores; and, if the frame variant is done, the origin and X direction set from points 1 and 2.

Related: #330 (face to plane, reopened), and the face-only pick issue filed alongside this one.
